payload.name: ResolveRelativeTimeFromMessageTimestamp
payload.description: When extracting or updating an event memory and a message contains a relative time phrase like 'last Sunday', 'yesterday', or 'last week', anchor the date using the message/session timestamp.
content: During candidate extraction, when a message contains a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last Sunday', 'yesterday', 'last week', 'two days ago'), resolve world_start from the message/session occurred_at timestamp: for 'last X' use the most recent X before that timestamp, for 'yesterday' use the day before, and so on.
Do not assign a fixed calendar date to a bare weekday that has no relative modifier (e.g., 'on Sunday') when the intended week is ambiguous; preserve the ambiguity instead of guessing a future date.

During UPDATE/MERGE or enrichment, do not overwrite an already-resolved event world_start with a later date taken from unrelated current-topic context unless a new message confirms the same event occurred again.

solves: Extraction or update of event memories frequently loses relative temporal references such as 'last Sunday', 'yesterday', or 'last week', producing a wrong or missing world_start that later fails time-based queries. In this diagnosis the phrase 'last Sunday' was reduced to a bare weekday and anchored after the message date. This Skill applies whenever a message timestamp is available to anchor such relative expressions; it does not apply to absolute dates or to messages without a usable timestamp anchor.
